text:
ConocoPhillips rose 0.84% today to $136.12, recovering from a sharp four-day decline that had knocked the stock down nearly $8 from mid-month highs. The bounce follows a stabilization in oil prices—US crude sitting at $89.53 per barrel today, up modestly from the lows earlier this week—and comes on the heels of Senate passage of the BAAJA permitting reform bill, which removes barriers for energy projects and infrastructure development that major producers like ConocoPhillips rely on to expand operations.

The broader backdrop remains mixed. Europe's energy crunch from depleted gas stocks and a weakening polar vortex could eventually support energy prices, but the recent geopolitical strain on the Strait of Hormuz corridor—which the IEA says has damaged confidence in Middle Eastern oil supply reliability—has not yet translated into a sustained oil rally strong enough to lift the stock back to its November highs.
